name: NFL Big Data Bowl - 1st Place (2020) - Pipeline Template
summary: Spatial trajectory, player-tracking, and football field-control solution template for NFL Big Data Bowl style tasks, modeled as a deterministic pipeline with spatial normalization, relative coordinate mapping, Voronoi or space-control features, time-to-contact and pursuit-angle features, spatial tensor formatting, CNN/GBDT trajectory or risk modeling, and CRPS or tackle-risk metric finalization.
dejargonized_summary: This template prepares player tracking data by flipping field coordinates to a common direction, expressing players relative to the ball carrier, building field-control features such as Voronoi areas, pursuit angles, time-to-contact, risk surfaces, and relative speeds, then trains a neural or gradient-boosted model and formats the football metric output.

inputs.name: raw_competition_data
inputs.constraints: Raw data for a Spatial Trajectory / 1D CNN task.

outputs.name: solution_predictions
outputs.constraints: Final predictions formatted for the benchmark metric.

use_when: The new task has the same broad problem type: spatial trajectory, football player tracking, field-control estimation, tackle-risk modeling, or 1D CNN/GBDT tracking prediction.

The available data supports the same ordered transformations and intermediate artifacts as the documented winning pipeline, including player coordinates, ball carrier or event anchors, velocities, accelerations, team direction, or field geometry.

Winning techniques include Voronoi diagrams, space-control surfaces, time-to-contact, pursuit angles, physics-informed pursuit or trajectory features, tackle risk, CNN sequence models, or gradient boosting over tracking features.
Offline processing is acceptable, including search, feature extraction, model ensembling, or post-processing stages.
do_not_use_when: The target task lacks the modality or metadata required by the early pipeline stages.
Strict real-time inference is required and the template depends on heavyweight extraction, search, ensembling, or test-time augmentation.
The evaluation metric rewards a fundamentally different output structure than the source competition.
applicability.key_insight: The load-bearing idea is the pipeline topology: spatial normalization and player-relative feature construction create a stable football tracking representation before CNN, GBDT, CRPS, or tackle-risk modeling.

swappable_stages.relative_coordinate_mapping: Can include ball-carrier-relative positions, velocities, accelerations, pursuit angle, time-to-contact, Voronoi space-control, or field-control risk surfaces.
swappable_stages.1d_cnn_architecture: Can be replaced by a CNN, MLP, GBDT, graph model, or ensemble over the same tracking feature contract.
swappable_stages.continuous_ranked_probability_score_crps: The final model, search policy, or ensemble can often be replaced if it preserves the same input/output contract and metric semantics.

applicability.scaling_notes: Scale bottlenecks are usually in feature extraction, graph/retrieval stages, neural inference, solver loops, and ensemble evaluation; cache intermediate artifacts when adapting this CDG.
failure_modes: Distribution shift breaks handcrafted thresholds, validation-derived weights, or post-processing rules.
Missing metadata prevents faithful construction of candidates, groups, windows, graphs, or cross-validation folds.
A weak first-stage recall, search, or representation step cannot be fully recovered by downstream rescoring or ensembling.

planning_constraints.subject: preserve_stage_order
planning_constraints.statement: Pipeline stages must execute in the documented order unless a replacement stage preserves the same input/output artifact contract.
planning_constraints.rationale: Downstream stages assume artifacts produced by earlier transformations.

planning_constraints.subject: validation_leakage_guard
planning_constraints.statement: Splits, folds, time ordering, and group boundaries from the source task must be respected when adapting the template.
planning_constraints.rationale: Many winning pipelines depend on leakage-safe validation or temporal grouping.

stages.name: Spatial normalization
stages.description: strictly flip all player X/Y coordinates and velocities so the offensive team is always moving left-to-right (numpy)
